Data Unit Samples: X-rays, Ledgers, and Owney

New: Owney data audit and visualization assessment ↓

Four complete records from api.si.edu/openaccess/api/v1.0/content/<id>. Each includes an image, selected key fields, and an expandable view of the complete JSON. All four share the same three-layer structure: freetext (human-written labels and paragraphs), indexedStructured (controlled fields), and descriptiveNonRepeating (identifiers, links, and images).

Sample 1 · X-ray · Albatross North Pacific Expedition, 1906

Film: Conger erebennus (conger eel). The full 10,173 × 2,503-pixel strip is available to download as a TIFF/JPEG. The film bears a lead-letter marker reading USNM 163468 and the handwritten identifier RAD105688-001.

Scientific name
Conger erebennus,Anguilliformes › Congridae
Collection date
15 October 1906
Expedition / vessel
Albatross North Pacific Expedition, 1906;Vessel: Albatross
Station
D 5065 (Site Number in freetext.notes)
Location
Ose Saki, S. 57.5° E., 7.5 miles (Suruga Bay, Japan)
Coordinates
35.0944, 138.658(indexedStructured.geoLocation.points)
Depth
386–430 m ("Depth (m)" in physicalDescription)
Identifiers
USNM 163468;Tin Tag 4339;RAD105688
Notes
A curator’s investigation: the ledger lists station D.5063, but the date does not match. After consulting the tin tag ledger, the station was corrected to D.5065. The record itself documents how it was corrected.
License
Metadata: CC0; image: CC0
This record includes an exact date, station number, coordinates, and depth: all the information needed to place the X-ray along the expedition’s route. The “tin tag ledger” mentioned in the notes shows that the Division of Fishes also has its own ledger system, although its scans are not currently available through Open Access.

Sample 2 · X-ray · Albatross Philippine Expedition, 1907–1910

Film: Petroscirtes variabilis (a blenny). Two fish on one film, USNM 138268, RAD120244-001.

Scientific name
Petroscirtes variabilis,Blenniidae
Collection date
9 May 1908
Expedition / vessel
Albatross Philippine Expedition, 1907–1910;Vessel: Albatross
Location
Capunuypugan Point, Generale Island, Mindanao (east coast of Mindanao)
Coordinates
None (only a place hierarchy: North Pacific Ocean › Philippines › Locality)
Preparation
Polyester (the X-ray film material); preparation count: 1
Notes
“The collection date is incorrect. The Albatross was not in this area in 1909, but was at this location in 1908, so the date was corrected to 9 May 1908.”
As in Sample 1, the notes trace a curator’s use of voyage logs to reconstruct and correct the record. Both records show that the Albatross’s location on a given date provides the underlying structure of this dataset: the X-rays are tied to the expedition’s route. This record has no coordinates, however, revealing uneven coordinate coverage. Mapping it requires resolving place names to locations.

Sample 3 · Ledger · Division of Birds, Volume 30, Catalog Nos. 152076–152100 · Ridgway in Florida, 1896

Image ID: media:NMNH-vol.030_152076-152100. This page contains 25 rows documenting collections made by Robert Ridgway (the Smithsonian’s first curator of birds) in south-central Florida in 1895–1896. At the upper right, “Ex. Carnegie Mus., 1904” appears beside a Carolina parakeet entry.

Of the 25 rows, 21 have matching API records, all of which point back to the same page image, confirming the mapping in both directions. Of the four missing entries, 152093 is explicitly recorded in the ledger as having been exchanged to the Carnegie Museum in 1904. The ledger records departures; the database records current holdings. In addition, the five specimens numbered 152095–152099, Conuropsis carolinensis (Carolina parakeet), were collected at Taylor’s Creek on 29 February 1896. The species became extinct in 1918; this page captures a day in the final two decades of its wild population.

Sample 4 · Ledger · Division of Mammals, Catalog Nos. 573126–573150 · Philippine Fruit Bat, 1988

Image ID: media:NMNH-573126-573150 (Division of Mammals image IDs contain only the catalog number range, without a volume number).

Scientific name
Cynopterus luzoniensis (Luzon short-nosed fruit bat), Chiroptera › Pteropodidae; alternative name: C. brachyotis luzoniensis
Collection date
24 February 1988
Collector
R. B. Utzurrum; field number RBU 227
Location
Gigmoto, 1 km N, 8.5 km W, Buadan River, Catanduanes, Philippines; coordinates: 13.8, 124.32
Preparation
Skeleton;Skull;Female
Notes
GenBank submission and publication reference: Roberts 2006, Mol. Ecol. 15(8), on the phylogeography of Philippine fruit bats. This bat’s DNA is already in a public database.
USNM
573133;Accession 378386
Compare this with the 1896 bird ledger page: the same Government Printing Office form was still in use 92 years later, but the notes now point to GenBank and journal DOIs. A handwritten entry connects to a genetic sequence, illustrating the span of time that a “museum of ledgers” could explore.

Sample 5 · Owney · Is this collection ready to visualize?

SMITHSONIAN OPEN ACCESS · DATA AUDIT · 22 SEPTEMBER 2026 (UTC)

Yes: a strong collection for an image-led explorer. The tag records are rich in photographs, physical details, and stories. A place-based view is feasible after geographic review; a timeline should preserve uncertainty. The records alone do not establish a complete, ordered travel route.

Owney was the Railway Mail Service’s canine mascot. His souvenirs include baggage checks, hotel keys, dog licenses, coins, advertising tokens, and medals. The museum also holds photographs, the preserved dog, and later commemorative objects. Museum overview ↗ · Tag themes ↗

422Search matches
403Postal Museum records
377Tag records audited
742Tag image entries · all CC0

Scope: one complete API search for Owney returned 422 distinct record IDs. The audit below covers the 377 National Postal Museum records whose titles contain both “Owney” and “tag.” This reproducible working set is not a claim that every surviving tag is digitized or that every match is a separate physical tag. The other 26 Postal Museum matches include seven photographs, eleven later exhibition blueprints, the dog, a spoon, and six modern commemorative objects. The remaining 19 results are library, archive, and research records; some are incidental keyword matches.

Bars count records with a populated field. Images total 742 distinct media IDs; 363 records have more than one image. “Other named people / organizations” excludes Owney himself.

How precise are the date fields?

Range / multiple days
26670.6%
Exact day
6116.2%
Year only
4110.9%
Approximate
61.6%
Month only
30.8%

246 records (65.3%) use the broad range 1888–1897. “Exact day” means the field’s format names one day, not that a visit has been independently verified. No date ranges were converted into invented single dates.

What the data contains, and how useful it is

InformationCoverage in tag setWhat it can supportWhat needs care
Images, object IDs, source links377 / 377 records; 742 imagesA searchable gallery, side-by-side inspection, and links back to evidence.Multiple images often show different views of the same object; count objects by record ID, not image count. Same titles can belong to different records.
Materials and dimensions377 / 377 for eachMaterial filters; size comparisons after parsing dimensions.Raw material labels include “metal” (213), “metal (brass)” (128), and a typo, “mdtal (brass).” Preserve raw values alongside cleaned categories. Dimensions mix inches, centimeters, fractions, and different axes.
Descriptions and inscriptions376 / 377 have descriptionsStories about donors, hotels, railroads, businesses, and inscriptions.Some records repeat general Owney history. Extract object-specific claims with their source passages; inscriptions and shape are not consistently separate fields.
Places338 / 377 (89.7%); 39 missingPlace filters now; a map after normalization and geocoding.0 / 377 contain coordinates. A geoLocation object often holds only text. Country, state, city, origin, and destination labels have different meanings; an associated place is not automatically a visit.
Dates377 / 377; 61 have a single-day formatAn interval timeline and a smaller set of reviewed dated events.A date can describe an object, a commemorated event, or a gift. Some exact dates exist only in the prose. Do not use the API’s update timestamps as historical dates.
People, organizations, themes34 / 377 name an entity other than Owney; 262 / 377 have topicsA curated network of donors, organizations, railroads, and places.Structured names are sparse and all 377 share the broad object type “Identifying artifacts.” Finer themes require manual classification or reviewed text extraction.
Reuse information377 / 377 metadata records and 742 / 742 tag image entries marked CC0Reusable images and metadata for this working set.Keep source links and credit lines with exported records.

Four records that show the opportunities and limits

A rich object with an uncertain date

Railroad Hotel Owney tag

Image: Smithsonian National Postal Museum · CC0

A hotel key token for room 33. The date field is 1888–1897 and the place field says Iowa; the description supplies Van Horne and a railroad. It supports a hotel-themed gallery and a candidate location, but no single travel date.

Date field
1888-1897
Place field
Iowa
Medium
metal (brass)

An exact date hidden in the description

St. Louis, Missouri Owney tag

Image: Smithsonian National Postal Museum · CC0

The date field gives only 1894. The description says postmaster J. B. Harlow gave Owney this coin on 24 May 1894; it also says the coin was minted for the 1893 Chicago World’s Fair. Keep the gift date separate from the coin’s commemorative date.

Object number
0.052985.19
Date field
1894
Place field
Missouri
Medium
metal

A strong candidate for a dated story point

Mankato, Minnesota Owney tag

Image: Smithsonian National Postal Museum · CC0

The date field gives 17 June 1895, and the description explicitly identifies a visit to Mankato, Minnesota, and donor J. C. Wise. This is good evidence for a dated visit after checking the record; the coordinates still need to be added.

Object number
0.052985.34
Date field
June 17, 1895
Place field
Minnesota

metal (brass)

A place name does not prove a visit

Chinook, Montana Owney tag

Image: Smithsonian National Postal Museum · CC0

The date field gives 14 May 1893, but the description says the railroads on the tag apparently did not pass through Chinook and the place where Owney received it is unknown. Display this as an association with uncertain geography.

Object number
0.052985.60
Date field
May 14, 1893
Place field
Montana
Medium
metal (brass)

Recommended visualization

Start with “Owney’s world through his tags”: an image gallery with filters for material, recorded place, date precision, and curated theme. Pair it with a map of reviewed place associations and an interval timeline. Selecting an object should reveal its photographs, original wording, and source record.

Material charts and the gallery are ready from the current fields. For a map, store the raw place, normalized place, geographic precision, meaning of the association, and geocoding source. For a timeline, store the raw date, start/end dates, date precision, event type, and supporting passage. Show uncertain associations explicitly; draw route lines only where separate evidence supports a sequence.

Two useful quality checks: the Lancaster House record gives 5 May 1896 and then says the presentation date is unknown. The Winnipeg license record includes both Canada and United States place labels. Keep these conflicts visible for review instead of silently resolving them.

Audit method, field paths, and sources

Retrieved 2026-09-22T04:49:43.813Z. Request: GET /openaccess/api/v1.0/search?q=Owney&rows=1000&start=0&sort=id. The API reported 422 matches and returned all 422 in one response; unique record IDs were checked. No media or museum filter was applied to the search. The tag set was then filtered locally by unitCode === "NPM" and case-insensitive whole-word title matches for “Owney” and “tag.” Counts describe this snapshot and may change.

The four example records were checked against /content/<id>; their content matched the search response. Dates were grouped by their literal format: a single calendar day, a year, a month, a c. approximation, or a range/multiple days. This measures available precision, not historical truth. Images count media entries with type Images; all 742 media IDs in the tag subset are distinct.

freetext supplies dates, named entities, notes, places, identifiers, and physical descriptions. indexedStructured supplies indexed places, date decades, topics, object type, and text-only geographic entries. descriptiveNonRepeating supplies record IDs, museum links, media, and usage statements. All download data and the page are credential-free; opening this file makes no authenticated API calls.

Sources: Smithsonian API documentation; National Postal Museum’s Owney overview; museum guide to tag themes; the linked object records and API snapshot. Recommendations are this page’s assessment of the inspected data.
